title: 105 CMR 700.004(B)(15): the conditions the Department adopted for pharmacist prescribing and dispensing of hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral hormonal contraceptives
subtopic: Regulatory conditions and registration exemption for pharmacist contraceptive prescribing
rule_summary: 105 CMR 700.004(B) is headed Exemptions from Requirement to Register. Its paragraph (15) provides that a registered pharmacist may prescribe and dispense hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral hormonal contraceptives to any person, in accordance with guidance issued by the department. Under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(15)(a) a registered pharmacist may prescribe and dispense a hormonal contraceptive patch or self-administered oral hormonal contraceptive regardless of whether the person has evidence of a previous prescription for a hormonal contraceptive patch or self-administered oral hormonal contraceptive, provided all requirements of 105 CMR 700.004(B)(15)(b) and (c) are met. Under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(15)(b) a registered pharmacist prescribing hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral hormonal contraceptives shall: 1. complete a training program approved by the board of registration in pharmacy that is related to prescribing hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral hormonal contraceptives prior to prescribing hormonal contraceptive patches or self-administered oral hormonal contraceptives; 2. provide a self-screening risk assessment tool that the patient shall use prior to the pharmacist prescribing the hormonal contraceptive patch or self-administered oral hormonal contraceptive; 3. refer the patient to the patient's primary care practitioner or reproductive health care practitioner, if applicable, upon prescribing and dispensing the hormonal contraceptive patch or self-administered oral hormonal contraceptive, or advise the patient to consult with a primary care practitioner or reproductive health care practitioner; 4. provide the patient with a written record of the hormonal contraceptive patch or self-administered oral hormonal contraceptive prescribed and dispensed; and 5. dispense the hormonal contraceptive patch or self-administered oral hormonal contraceptive to the patient as soon as practicable after the pharmacist issues the prescription. Under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(15)(c) a pharmacist shall not require a patient to schedule an appointment with the pharmacist for the prescribing or dispensing of a hormonal contraceptive patch or self-administered oral hormonal contraceptive.
exam_relevance: Tests which of the statutory directions the Department adopted in regulation, that the regulation grants the authority in accordance with Department guidance, and that the authority sits among the exemptions from the requirement to register.

authority.name: Registered pharmacist prescribing and dispensing of hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral hormonal contraceptives

exceptions: Under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(15)(b)3 the pharmacist may advise the patient to consult with a primary care practitioner or reproductive health care practitioner instead of referring the patient, and the referral is qualified by the words if applicable.
common_confusions: Reading into 105 CMR 700.004(B)(15) the clinical-visit prohibition that M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19F(c)(ii)(B) directs the rules to contain; paragraph (15) states no clinical-visit time frame and no such prohibition.
Overlooking that paragraph (15) grants the authority in accordance with guidance issued by the department.
Treating the absence of a previous prescription as the only condition; 105 CMR 700.004(B)(15)(a) makes the authority subject to all requirements of subparagraphs (b) and (c).
verification_notes: Read 105 CMR 700.004(B), including the heading and paragraph (15)(a) through (c), in the current 105 CMR 700.000 publication on mass.gov (PDF last updated 2024-02-02) on 2026-09-16.
